steps: IV 0.9% saline resuscitation first (fluid deficit is large); careful in young/cardiac/renal.
Fixed-rate IV insulin infusion (~0.1 U/kg/h); continue basal insulin if on it.
Replace potassium once K <5.5 and urine output adequate (insulin drives K intracellularly).
Add dextrose when glucose <14 mmol/L; monitor ketones, glucose, K, pH hourly.
Find and treat the precipitant; do not stop insulin infusion until ketones cleared and eating.

drugRefs.dose: ~1 L over the first hour, then titrated to deficit/haemodynamics
drugRefs.why: Corrects the large fluid deficit and improves perfusion; give before/alongside insulin. Caution in young, cardiac or renal patients.

drugRefs.duration: until ketones cleared, acidosis resolved and patient eating
drugRefs.why: Switches off ketogenesis and lowers glucose. Continue long-acting basal insulin if already prescribed.

drugRefs.dose: add per serum K⁺ (e.g. 40 mmol/L when K⁺ 3.5–5.5)
drugRefs.why: Insulin drives K⁺ intracellularly; replace once K⁺ <5.5 mmol/L and urine output is adequate. Withhold if K⁺ >5.5 or anuric.
Lets the insulin infusion continue to clear ketones without causing hypoglycaemia.

confirm: Hyperglycaemia + ketonaemia/ketonuria + high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis. Often a precipitant (infection, missed insulin, new T1DM).
